- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast slope or shift mean downward by 1–2%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast peak at 1–2% above prior high.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days falling >1% from prior), model underestimates drop; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- When sentiment is neutral or positive (≥ 0.2) and model is flat or rising, model often misses downward shock; add 1–2% buffer for volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early days (1–3 days) and underestimates late days (last 5–7); apply asymmetric smoothing: reduce first 3 days, increase last 3 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 2+ consecutive -1.0), model tends to ignore sentiment; force a 0.5–1.0% downward bias in forecast.
